title: Factoring reduced algebraic spaces through closed subspaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subspace. A closed subspace means a subfunctor whose inclusion becomes a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $Y$ is reduced, meaning that its etale scheme charts have no nonzero nilpotents in their local rings. For every $S$-morphism $f:Y\to X$, there is a morphism $g:Y\to Z$ with $ig=f$ if and only if $|f|(|Y|)\subseteq |Z|$ in the atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Such a factorization is unique.

source.place: Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction); uniqueness because a closed subspace is a subsheaf.

proof.text: If $f=i\circ g$, then $|f|(y)=|i|(|g|(y))$ for every point class $y$, so the point-image containment is necessary. Since $Z\subseteq X$ is a subfunctor, each $Z(T)\to X(T)$ is injective. Consequently two morphisms $Y\to Z$ with composite $f$ agree on every scheme test and are equal. It remains to construct a factorization from the point-image containment.

source.place: Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction), proof; source-atlas pullback form of the same scheme-local argument.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the assumed meaning of reducedness, $V$ is reduced. The closed subspace $Z$ is an algebraic space over $S$ by [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace] (a subfunctor with closed-immersion inclusion is equivalently an algebraic space with that property). Put $C=V\times_{X,f\circ b}Z$ and let $c:C\to V$ be the projection. The scheme-test definition of the closed subspace makes $C$ a scheme and $c$ a closed immersion. Apply the arbitrary-base-change point-image identity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] to $Z\to X$ and $f\circ b:V\to X$: its image is $|f\circ b|^{-1}(|Z|)=|V|$, by the assumed containment. Thus $c$ is surjective on scheme points.

source.place: Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction), proof; source-atlas pullback form of the same scheme-local argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to the closed immersion $c:C\to V$ and the identity of the reduced scheme $V$. The preceding surjectivity is exactly the required image containment. It gives $s:V\to C$ with $c\circ s=1_V$. This $s$ is over $S$ because $c$ is over $S$ and $c\circ s=1_V$. Composing $s$ with $C\to Z$ gives $k:V\to Z$ satisfying $i\circ k=f\circ b$ by the defining pullback equation.

source.place: Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction), proof; source-atlas pullback form of the same scheme-local argument.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in Y(T)$, [lem-a1-representable-etale-fppf-local-lifting] applied to $b$ gives an fppf covering $v:T^{\prime}\to T$ and $a:T^{\prime}\to V$ with $b(a)=y|_{T^{\prime}}$. Set $z^{\prime}=k(a)\in Z(T^{\prime})$. Both restrictions of $z^{\prime}$ to $T^{\prime}\times_TT^{\prime}$ have image $f(y)$ restricted there, so they coincide by the sectionwise injectivity of $Z\subseteq X$. Since $Z$ is an algebraic space [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace], hence an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], its sheaf axiom gives a unique $z\in Z(T)$; its image is $f(y)$ since these sections of the sheaf $X$ agree on the cover. The unique-lift property makes the assignment $y\mapsto z$ commute with every restriction $T_1\to T$, since restriction of $z$ is a lift of $f(y)|_{T_1}$. These assignments therefore define an $S$-morphism $g:Y\to Z$ with $i\circ g=f$.

source.place: Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction), proof; source-atlas pullback form of the same scheme-local argument.
